| τὴν δ’ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσεφώνεε νήδυμος Ὕπνος (14.242, whole-line reply-formula) | "To her answering spoke sweet Sleep:" | "In answer sweet Sleep spoke to her:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο), "slumber"; follows the table’s τὸν δ’ ἀπαμειβόμενος προσεφώνεε Τεῦκρος ἀμύμων "To him answering spoke" / "In answer … spoke to him" |
| νήδυμος Ὕπνος (14.242, Sleep’s stock epithet; meaning not known) | "sweet Sleep" | "sweet Sleep" (+ note: meaning and origin not known; "sweet" is traditional) | "soft", "gentle", "deep"; keeps the Odyssey’s and the Iliad’s νήδυμος ὕπνος "sweet sleep" |
| τὸν δὲ δολοφρονέουσα προσηύδα πότνια Ἥρη (14.300, masculine form of 14.197) | "And to him, with guile in her mind, spoke lady Hera:" | "Then lady Hera, with guile in her mind, spoke to him:" | "deceitfully", "craftily"; the masculine-object counterpart of the table’s τὴν δὲ δολοφρονέουσα (14.197) |
| τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε βοῶπις πότνια Ἥρη (14.263, whole-line reply-formula with αὖτε) | "Him then in turn addressed ox-eyed lady Hera:" | "Then ox-eyed lady Hera spoke to him in turn:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); the αὖτε counterpart of the fixed τὸν δ’ ἠμείβετ’ ἔπειτα βοῶπις πότνια Ἥρη |
| ἀάατον (Στυγὸς ὕδωρ, 14.271; meaning not known) | "inviolable" | "inviolable" (+ note: meaning not known; "not to be harmed" is the traditional gloss) | "harmless" (the Odyssey’s 21.91 guess, wrong for an oath), "unfailing", "dread" (reserved for δεινός) |
| μαρμαρέη (ἅλα μαρμαρέην, 14.273) | "gleaming" | "gleaming" | "sparkling" (kept for μαρμαίροντα, 20), "shimmering", "glittering" |
| ὑποταρτάριοι (θεοί, 14.279) | "beneath Tartarus" | "beneath Tartarus" | "in Tartarus", "of Tartarus", "underworld" |
| ἄϊστος (14.258) | "unseen" | "never to be seen again" / "vanished from sight" | "unknown", "invisible", "lost" |
| Χάριτες (Χαρίτων μίαν ὁπλοτεράων, 14.267) | "one of the younger Graces" | "one of the younger Graces" | "Charites", "Gracious ones"; ὁπλότερος "younger" |
